Hello scientific writers! In this video I'm going to show you an easy way to quickly customize your NIH biosketch. Hi, this is Brian from the Grants and Publications YouTube channel. Now making a customized NIH biosketch for every application is a good idea. When you customize your biosketch for each project it helps the reviewer see why you are uniquely qualified to carry out the role you have in that proposed project. And there are different parts that you have to customize. There's the personal statement, and then the contributions to science might be a little bit different depending on what you're doing in various projects. You might want to highlight different publications or research products that you produced in the past. So I'm going to show you how to use some software from the National Library of Medicine that's called SciENcv to make your biosketch very quickly. Now you can just type the information in to this template that the NIH provides, which is in a Word document format, and then just save it with a different name, but if you would like to try the SciENcv, I find it very handy because it does more than just an NIH biosketch. We'll look at that right now and I'll show you what I mean. All right so this is what the NCBI webpage looks like. And this is where we're going to enter the system to get to SciENcv. You need to have an account with NCBI. So just go up here to sign in. Alright so now I'm signed in I'm going to go up here to the top of the screen and click my NCBI. One thing you want to start out with is My Bibliography. So click manage My Bibliography. What you're going to do is add all of your citations. So I'm going to search from Pubmed and I will enter my last name and initials and I will search. Okay so here are some of my publications, so I can select those and I can click add to My Bibliography. Not all of my publications were found in Pubmed so I'm going to add some of them manually. So we can just type in the title of the article, the authors, and you can just add more authors if you have multiple authors, the journal, the publication date, the volume, the issue, the page, the URL, the unique id, the type of unique id if you have one of those. So here are a lot of choices; there's the doi and orcid, etc. So you see all the choices you have here. Now recall when you're filling out your biosketch that you can add publications or research products. So what are research products? They can include but are not limited to: audio or video products, conference proceedings, patents, data and research materials, databases, educational aids or curricula, instruments or equipment, models, protocols, software or netware, or interim research products such as preprints. Now one of the nice things about My Bibliography is it's not only for publications. You can add these other research products as well. So how do you add other research products? You can just go here to add citations, and say manually, then choose the type of citation to create. So you can add a book or chapter, a meeting abstract, a presentation, a patent, a dataset or a database, software, preprint, or other. Select the type and fill out the fields as appropriate. Once you have your bibliography complete go back to my NCBI. And now we're going to go here to SciENcv and we're going to say manage SciENcv. And you can say create a new document. Give the document a name and then you can choose the format. You can do an NIH biosketch, an NIH fellowship biosketch, you can also do an NSF biosketch, an NSF current and pending support, or an IES biosketch. So we're going to go with an NIH biosketch. And then we could say start with a blank document, or start with an existing document, or an external source such as ERA Commons, but we're going to just start with a blank document, and we're going to keep it private for now.
